title: Noetherian coherent finiteness and ascending chains on spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Modules, tensor pullback and direct image are on these ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Locally Noetherian means locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-locnoeth]; Noetherian means additionally quasi-compact and quasi-separated (quasi-compact diagonal). Coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. If $B$ is a Noetherian algebraic space and $f:X\to B$ is quasi-separated and of finite type [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], then $X$ is Noetherian. On a locally Noetherian algebraic space, an $\mathcal O_X$-module is coherent if and only if it is quasi-coherent of finite type, and if and only if it is finitely presented (etale locally a cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules). On a Noetherian $X$, quasi-coherent submodules of any coherent module satisfy the ascending chain condition. In particular every nonempty set of quasi-coherent ideal sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$ has a maximal member for inclusion.

source.place: Tags 07UB (lemma-coherent-Noetherian), 07UJ (lemma-acc-coherent); local Noetherian inheritance is spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04ZK (lemma-locally-finite-type-locally-noetherian), together with finite-type quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness.

proof.text: First prove local Noetherian inheritance. Take any etale scheme chart $T\to X$ and a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to B$. The fibre product $W=T\times_BV$ is a scheme and $W\to T$ is surjective etale, by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The composite $W\to T\to X$ is etale: on each scheme test it is a composite of etale scheme maps, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] applies. Consequently $W\to V$ is one of the compatible chart maps in the finite-type hypothesis [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], and is locally of finite type. The scheme $V$ is locally Noetherian by the chart meaning of that hypothesis on $B$. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to $W\to V$, then [lem-trf-etale-local-noetherian-descent] to $W\to T$. This makes every $T$ locally Noetherian, as required. No quasi-compactness of $T,V,W$ is needed here.

For global Noetherianity, first compare the two forms of quasi-compactness of a space used here: a representable surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-compactness of the point space $|\cdot|$ in the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. If $h_{U_0}\to B$ is surjective etale with $U_0$ quasi-compact, then $|U_0|\to|B|$ is surjective and continuous by the definition of that final topology, so $|B|$ is quasi-compact; conversely [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] gives an affine atlas. Thus choose an affine surjective etale atlas $V\to B$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. Finite type includes quasi-compactness [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]; since $V$ is affine, the point space of $Y=X\times_BV$ is quasi-compact, in agreement with the affine-test criterion [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. Choose an affine surjective etale atlas $U\to Y$ by the same atlas lemma. The map $Y\to X$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and $U\to X$ is therefore surjective etale. For etaleness, test on a scheme and apply the scheme composition clause of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]; surjectivity follows by lifting a point successively through the two covers. Thus $U\to X$ exhibits quasi-compactness, using the atlas characterization in [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests], and $|X|$ is quasi-compact by the comparison above. Finally, the diagonal of a space is taken in sheaves on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$, whose product is the fibre product over the final object $S$; so quasi-separatedness of $B$ means that $B\to S$ is quasi-separated. Compose the quasi-separated morphisms $X\to B$ and $B\to S$ by [lem-sfb-space-quasiseparated-test-calculus]; hence $X\to S$ is quasi-separated. Together with step 1 this proves that $X$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 04ZK together with spaces-properties.tex lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover and quasi-separated composition

proof.text: Now let $X$ be any locally Noetherian algebraic space. If $F$ is quasi-coherent, its restrictions to scheme charts are quasi-coherent by the local-presentation definition [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Identify each chart restriction with a Zariski quasi-coherent scheme module by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Finite type on the two sites agrees by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison]. All these chart schemes are locally Noetherian. Thus [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes their modules coherent exactly when they are of finite type. Finite type is a local condition: restricting the local finite generating epimorphisms to slice sites preserves them, and generating epimorphisms on a covering family are exactly the local generators required in its definition. Hence $F$ is coherent in the chart convention of the statement if and only if it is quasi-coherent of finite type. This also gives coherence of $\mathcal O_X$, since it has its one-generator free presentation on every chart.

A finite presentation $\mathcal O^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O^{\oplus n}\to F\to0$ is a presentation of the form allowed in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], so a finitely presented module is quasi-coherent. Its last map gives finite type. Step 3 therefore makes every finitely presented module coherent. This implication only uses the definitions of local presentation and finite type.

Conversely let $F$ be quasi-coherent of finite type. On any locally Noetherian scheme chart $T\to X$, use [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] and [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] to obtain a Zariski quasi-coherent module $G$ of finite type. For an affine open $A\subseteq T$, its ring $R=\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_T)$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], and $\Gamma(A,G)$ is finite over $R$ by clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]. Apply [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation] to this module, and clause (b) of the affine criterion to conclude that $G|_A$ is finitely presented. These affine opens cover $T$. The exact finiteness comparison then makes $F|_{T_{\mathrm{et}}}$ finitely presented. Such local finite presentations on the chart cover of $X$ are precisely finite presentation on its small etale site. Together with steps 3 and 4 this proves all three equivalent conditions.

proof.text: For ACC, let $X$ be Noetherian, $F$ coherent, and $F_1\subseteq F_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F$ quasi-coherent submodules. Since $|X|$ is quasi-compact (step 2 compares the two forms of quasi-compactness), choose an affine surjective etale atlas $p:U\to X$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. It is a locally Noetherian scheme by the chart hypothesis on $X$, and is quasi-compact since affine, hence Noetherian as a scheme. Etale pullback is restriction to the localized site [def-trf-algebraic-space]. It preserves submodule inclusions and their equality as subsheaves on that site. By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] and the exactness clause of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison], this gives a chain of quasi-coherent Zariski submodules of the coherent scheme module corresponding to $p^*F$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-acc-quasi-coherent] on $U$ to obtain one $n$ such that the restrictions of $F_m$ and $F_n$ agree as submodules of $p^*F$ for every $m\ge n$. To descend equality, take any chart $T\to X$ and section $s\in F_m(T)$. On the surjective etale cover $T\times_XU\to T$ this section lies in $F_n$. These local sections of $F_n$ agree on overlaps, because their images agree in $F$ and $F_n\hookrightarrow F$ is a monomorphism. The sheaf axiom glues them to a section of $F_n(T)$ whose image is $s$. Thus $F_m(T)\subseteq F_n(T)$ for every $T$; the reverse inclusion comes from the chain. This proves global stabilization.

Finally $\mathcal O_X$ is coherent by step 3. A quasi-coherent ideal sheaf is a quasi-coherent submodule of this module, so step 6 applies to increasing sequences of such ideals. If a nonempty set of quasi-coherent ideals had no maximal member, choose a first member $I_0$ and, recursively, a strictly larger member $I_{r+1}$ in that same set. Classical choice permits this recursion in the fixed universe. It produces a strictly increasing sequence, contradicting step 6. Therefore every such nonempty set has a maximal member. The argument also includes $X=\varnothing$, where the only ideal sheaf is the zero sheaf.
